---
argmap-version: 0.2
title: "Tutorial: linked (AND) vs convergent (separate lines)"
description: "The same claim, the same two grounds and the same strength, joined two ways. In the first block one line takes both grounds under AND, which says neither ground alone would do. In the second two separate lines take one ground each, which says either alone would do. The syntax difference is one word; the solved values are far apart, and the second is much the higher, because independent lines accumulate while a conjunction is only as available as its scarcest conjunct. The test that decides which you have: could you delete one ground and still make the argument?"
---

# ===========================================================================
# THE TEST, and it is the only thing to remember:
#
#     Write AND only if NEITHER conjunct alone suffices.
#     If either alone would carry the claim, write separate lines.
#
# Getting it backwards is the most common structural mistake in a first
# draft, and it is invisible: both versions parse, both render, and both
# produce a plausible-looking number. The flagship map shipped a four-way
# AND for a year where the source plainly said "any one of these suffices";
# the repair note is still in the file.
#
# WHICH WAY THE ERROR RUNS. A false AND UNDERSTATES: it makes the claim
# hostage to the least likely ground. A false pair of convergent lines
# OVERSTATES, and worse, it overstates in a way that grows: three separate
# lines that secretly share a cause stack toward certainty while deserving
# one line's worth of support. When in doubt, AND is the safer error, and
# naming the shared cause as its own statement is better than either.
# ===========================================================================

# ---- block 1: LINKED. One line, both grounds, AND. ------------------------
# The claim here is that the two together are what point inside. A key with
# no reason to use it is a caretaker; a reason with no key is a stranger.

@key [The suspect held a key to the studio] 0.8:
@motive [The suspect had a reason to want the canvas gone] 0.7:
@inside [The theft was done from inside the household]:  # check: 0.7
$linked [neither the key nor the reason alone puts them inside] 0.75 @inside | @key AND @motive:

# ---- block 2: CONVERGENT. Two lines, one ground each. ---------------------
# Same grounds, same strength, and now each is claimed to be sufficient on
# its own. Nothing about the words changed; the structure did.

@key2 [The suspect held a key to the studio] 0.8:
@motive2 [The suspect had a reason to want the canvas gone] 0.7:
@inside2 [The theft was done from inside the household]:  # check: 0.7
$conv-key [a key on the night is enough on its own] 0.75 @inside2 | @key2:
$conv-motive [a motive that strong is enough on its own] 0.75 @inside2 | @motive2:

# ---- the numbers side by side ---------------------------------------------
# Solved 2026-08-04 (D36 defaults, solve_map.py):
#
#   linked      @inside   check 0.70 -> 0.700
#   convergent  @inside2  check 0.70 -> 0.882
#
# Eighteen points of credence rest on one word, and the author's own check
# is met exactly in one block and overshot badly in the other. That is the
# whole argument for spending a minute on the test above before writing the
# line: an AND you did not mean does not look like an error, it looks like a
# cautious estimate, and a convergent pair you did not mean looks like a
# well-supported claim.
#
# Two smaller things in the same readout, both worth noticing once:
#
# - The two grounds solve identically in both blocks (@key 0.796, @motive
#   0.697). All the difference is downstream, at the conclusion. Structure
#   changed what the grounds BUY, not what they are worth.
# - The convergent block does not reach the sum of its parts. Each line is a
#   floor, and where one is silent the other can still speak, which is why
#   two lines at 0.75 land near 0.88 rather than at 0.94 or at 1.5.
#
# When the honest answer is "either would do, but they overlap", neither
# block above is right. Name the overlap as a statement and condition both
# lines on it, or partition them with an explicit `AND ~@other-route`.
